draft.title: ADR: Start Spotify from SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN, fall back to the browser sign-in, drop the sp_dc cookie
draft.context: `SpotifyClient.initialAuth` sends a GET for the authorize URL with `Cookie: sp_dc=$SPOTIFY_SP_DC` (`src/main/scala/client/SpotifyClient.scala:73`). That cookie gives full access to the web session, and it's the only reason a start finishes without anyone at a browser. The configured `SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN` is only read as a fallback inside `renew`, and `getOrRefresh` always goes to `initialAuth` when there's no session. The config also requires `SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN` (`application.conf:4`). Removing the cookie on its own would make every start wait for a browser.
draft.decision:
Sign-in stays lazy, at the first Spotify call, so the existing poll loop and its retry are unchanged. Only the `None` branch of `getOrRefresh` changes: it now calls a new `signIn`.
- `signIn`: if `creds.configuredRefreshToken` (the configured token, trimmed, `None` when blank) is set, swap it at `POST /api/token` with `grant_type=refresh_token`. If Spotify answers 4xx (`SpotifyTokenError.Rejected`), log a warning that has no token value in it, then run `initialAuth`. If no token is set, go straight to `initialAuth`.
- `initialAuth` no longer requests the authorize URL. It logs the URL, waits on the callback `Deferred`, then exchanges the code as before. Nothing reads `SPOTIFY_SP_DC` any more, so a value left in `.env` does nothing.
- The startup swap and `renew` share one private `refreshWith`, which raises the typed `SpotifyTokenError`. `renew` keeps its current behaviour: it uses the session's refresh token, and if Spotify refuses, the poll fails.
- `refreshToken` stays a `String`, defaulting to `""`, and blank means "not configured". This keeps every caller and test compiling, and treats an unset variable and an empty `SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN=` from `.env` the same way.
- Order: the startup swap lands before the cookie is removed, so no release ever waits on a browser at every start.
draft.components:
- `Main` → `SpotifyClient.resource` (unchanged) → `SyncEngine` poller → `SpotifyClient.getPlaybackState` → `authorised` → `getOrRefresh` → **`signIn`** → (`refreshWith("Refresh Token Exchange")` | **`initialAuth`**) → accounts.spotify.com `/api/token`.
- `initialAuth` → `authCodeDeferred.get`, which is completed by `callbackRoutes` (unchanged) when the browser hits `127.0.0.1:7070/callback`.
- `renew` → `refreshWith("Renew")`.
- `SpotifyCredentials` (domain) gains the pure `configuredRefreshToken`.
- New `client.SpotifyTokenError` (sealed), plus a pure classifier `SpotifyTokenError.of(call, status, body)`.
- Docs: README, `.env.example`, `docs/how-it-works.md` §1 (sequence diagram and bullets), and the `docs/roadmap.md` item ticked off.
draft.contracts:
- Env `SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN`: required → optional. Unset or blank means no token. Additive, since it only loosens.
- Env `SPOTIFY_SP_DC`: no longer read anywhere. Removed from `.env.example` and the docs. Any value left in the environment is ignored.
- Config key `spotify.refresh-token`: `${SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN}` → `${?SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN}`. When it's missing, the case-class default `""` is used. Additive.
- Shared type `domain.spotify.SpotifyCredentials`: `refreshToken: String` gains the default `""` and a `def configuredRefreshToken: Option[String]`. Source-compatible, and the circe codec shape is unchanged. Additive.
- New type `client.SpotifyTokenError` (a `RuntimeException`, so existing `intercept[RuntimeException]` tests still hold). Additive.
- `SpotifyClient` API: adds `def signIn: F[String]`. The signatures of `initialAuth`, `renew` and `getOrRefresh` are unchanged. The `"Authorize"` call name for TLS failures goes away (no authorize request is sent any more), and `"Refresh Token Exchange"` replaces it.
- Outbound HTTP: no more `GET accounts.spotify.com/authorize` and no `Cookie` header. Adds one `POST /api/token` with `grant_type=refresh_token` at startup when a token is configured.
- No change to settings JSON, the UI endpoints, the callback server or the scopes.
draft.failureModes:
Carried by `SpotifyTokenError` (sealed): `Rejected(call, status, body)` for any 4xx, and `Failed(call, status, body)` for any other non-success status.
- **Startup swap**: `Rejected` is recoverable. It logs a warning and the browser sign-in follows. `Failed`, a transport error or a `SpotifyTlsFailure("Refresh Token Exchange")` propagate to the poll. `SyncEngine` logs "Spotify Poll Failed" and the session stays `None`, so the next tick retries `signIn`. The browser is not used for these, because a 5xx or a network outage says nothing about the token.
- **Browser sign-in**: the code exchange fails as it does today (a `RuntimeException`, or `SpotifyTlsFailure("Code Exchange")`), the poll fails, and the next tick logs a fresh URL. Waiting on the `Deferred` never times out, which is intended.
- **Renew during a run**: `Rejected` or `Failed` fail that poll, as today (out of scope to change).
- Nothing in this change is fatal at startup. A blank or missing token can no longer cause a config error.
- Secrets: the token value never appears in any error message or log line. `body` is Spotify's own error JSON, which doesn't echo the token. Never log `SpotifyCredentials` or `AppConfig`, because their `toString` includes the secrets.
draft.config: No new settings. `spotify.refresh-token` becomes optional (`${?SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN}`, default `""`). At startup, pureconfig still requires `client-id` and `client-secret`. A blank or whitespace-only token is treated as absent by `configuredRefreshToken`, not rejected, so `SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN=` copied straight from `.env.example` works. `LightShowConfig.problems` is untouched.
draft.observability:
All of these come from the `client.SpotifyClient` logger:
- INFO `Signed in to Spotify with the configured refresh token`. No fields.
- WARN `Spotify rejected the configured refresh token (status: <status>); signing in through the browser instead`. Fields: the HTTP status only. Never the token or the response body.
- INFO `Please visit: <authorize URL>` (unchanged text). Fields: `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `scope`, `state`. No secrets.
- INFO `Signed in to Spotify through the browser`, after the code exchange succeeds.
- Unchanged: INFO `Renewed the Spotify access token`, and ERROR `Spotify Poll Failed: <SpotifyTokenError message>` from `SyncEngine`, whose message holds the call, the status and Spotify's body.
alternatives: Sign in eagerly inside `SpotifyClient.resource`: Hue setup would wait for browser approval, and a 5xx at startup would stop the app instead of being retried on the next poll.

Make `refreshToken: Option[String]`: more precise types, but every `SpotifyCredentials(...)` call in four test suites would change, and `""` from `.env` still needs normalising. The default-`""` approach plus `configuredRefreshToken` gives the same behaviour as a smaller change.

Inject a `Logger[F]` into `SpotifyClient` so tests can capture logs: this adds a fifth constructor parameter (a `using` clause) and touches every construction site. Tests attach a logback `ListAppender` to the `client.SpotifyClient` logger instead (logback is already on the classpath), and production code doesn't change.

slices.title: 1. Make SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN optional and add SpotifyTokenError
slices.delivers: Contracts first. `application.conf` uses `${?SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN}`, `SpotifyCredentials.refreshToken` defaults to "", `configuredRefreshToken` is added, and the new `SpotifyTokenError` type comes with its `of` classifier. `renew` raises `SpotifyTokenError` through the shared `refreshWith`. With no token set, the app now starts without a config error and signs in on first use, still through the existing flow.
acceptanceCriteria: The shipped application.conf loads with SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN unset, empty or set, and it gives the same AppConfig with or without SPOTIFY_SP_DC in the source
`configuredRefreshToken` is None for an empty or whitespace-only token, and otherwise is the token with surrounding whitespace removed
Each 4xx status maps to Rejected and every other unsuccessful status to Failed, and no error message contains the refresh token sent
The existing renewal tests still pass: polls keep succeeding after an expired access token is rejected (AC 7)
slices.testStrategy: Extend LightShowConfigSpec's "shipped application.conf" test into a table over the token unset, empty and set, each with and without SPOTIFY_SP_DC. A ScalaCheck property for `configuredRefreshToken` over blank and non-blank strings. A ScalaCheck property for `SpotifyTokenError.of` over generated statuses, and one that the message of a renew failure never contains the generated refresh token. The SpotifyClientSpec renewal tests stay as they are.

slices.title: 2. Start from the configured refresh token, falling back to the browser
slices.delivers: Adds `signIn`, and the `None` branch of `getOrRefresh` calls it. A valid token starts the lights with no sign-in URL logged. A rejected token logs a warning without its value, then falls back to the browser sign-in. 5xx and transport failures are retried on the next poll. The README marks SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN as optional, and how-it-works §1 describes the startup swap.
acceptanceCriteria: With a valid token, the first poll sends exactly one POST /api/token with grant_type=refresh_token, plays, and logs no 'Please visit' line (AC 2)

With the token rejected (400 invalid_grant), the log has one WARN saying the configured refresh token was rejected, no log event anywhere contains the token value, and then 'Please visit' is logged; completing /callback?code=… leads to a successful poll (AC 3)
With the token unset or empty, no refresh_token grant is sent and 'Please visit' is logged; completing the callback leads to a successful poll (AC 1)
A 503 from the startup swap fails that poll without logging a sign-in URL, and the next poll tries the swap again
Renewing during a run behaves as before (AC 7)
slices.testStrategy: In SpotifyClientSpec, a table of configured token × token-endpoint answer (valid, 400, 503, none), run against the fake Spotify built with Client.fromHttpApp. It records requests and grant types, and captures logs with a testkit `Logs` helper that attaches a logback ListAppender to `client.SpotifyClient` inside a Resource. Assertions match on a client_id unique to each test. The browser approval is simulated by running `callbackRoutes` with `/callback?code=` once the URL has been logged. SyncEngineRunSpec under TestControl shows the lights following playback in each of the three cases. Update the TLS test 'signing in against an untrusted certificate' so it expects 'Refresh Token Exchange' and no client secret sent.

slices.title: 3. Drop the sp_dc cookie and its docs
slices.delivers: `initialAuth` no longer requests the authorize URL. It logs the URL and waits on the callback. Nothing reads SPOTIFY_SP_DC. README, .env.example and how-it-works no longer mention it, and the roadmap item is ticked off.
acceptanceCriteria: Across every sign-in path (valid, rejected, absent token), no request recorded by the fake Spotify carries a Cookie header, and none goes to /authorize (AC 4)
`rg -i 'sp_dc'` over src/, README.md, .env.example and docs/how-it-works.md finds nothing (AC 4, 5, 6)
Startup, sign-in and playback behave the same whether or not SPOTIFY_SP_DC is in the environment, because nothing reads it (AC 5)
Browser sign-in still completes once the callback receives the code, and the code exchange sends grant_type=authorization_code (AC 1)
slices.testStrategy: Rewrite the SpotifyClientSpec and SpotifyTlsSpec sign-in tests so they complete the code through `callbackRoutes` (or the Deferred) instead of a fake /authorize route. Add an assertion over all recorded requests that there is no Cookie header and no /authorize path. Drop the TLS 'Authorize' naming assertion, and keep 'Code Exchange'. The docs are checked by an rg in review rather than a test, since DocsSpec was removed on purpose in c383e29.

```scala
import org.http4s.Status

/** Spotify's token endpoint refused a request. Messages carry Spotify's answer, never the token sent. */

}
```

findings.problem: The design says that when the code exchange fails, "the poll fails, and the next tick logs a fresh URL", as if the user can retry. They can't. `authCodeDeferred` is a single `Deferred` made once in `SpotifyClient.resource` (SpotifyClient.scala:176). After the first callback it stays completed, so on the next tick `initialAuth` logs a new URL, `authCodeDeferred.get` hands back the same spent code at once, the exchange fails again, and this repeats every poll. Approving the new URL does nothing, because `callbackRoutes` calls `deferred.complete`, which is a no-op the second time. Today the cookie mostly hid this. Once the cookie is gone, browser sign-in is the only path for users without a token and the fallback for rejected tokens (AC 1 and AC 3), so one failed exchange (an expired code, a double click, a 5xx) means restarting the app. That contradicts "The app doesn't stop with an error in either fallback case".
findings.suggestion: Either fix it within the change's scope, or state the limitation instead of claiming a retry. A fix could hold the code in a `Ref[F, Option[Deferred[F, String]]]` (or a queue) that `initialAuth` creates fresh for each attempt and `callbackRoutes` completes. Changing what the callback route completes isn't changing the callback server's behaviour. Add a test: a failed exchange, then a second approval, then a successful poll.

findings.problem: `Rejected` covers every 4xx, and every `Rejected` from the startup swap is read as "the configured refresh token was rejected", with a fallback to the browser. 429 Too Many Requests is a 4xx that says nothing about the token. So is 401/400 `invalid_client` (wrong client id or secret). On a 429 the app logs a misleading warning and makes the user approve in a browser for no reason. On `invalid_client` it blames the token and sends the user to a browser flow whose code exchange will fail too, and given the Deferred issue above, it then loops. The design's own reasoning ("a 5xx or a network outage says nothing about the token") applies to these cases as well.
findings.suggestion: Treat only Spotify's token-specific answer as `Rejected` for the startup swap: status 400 with `error: invalid_grant`. Classify 429 and other 4xx as `Failed`, so they're retried on the next poll. Add 429 and `invalid_client` rows to the slice 2 table and to the `of` property.

findings.section: Slices 1 and 3 — tests for AC 4 and AC 5
findings.problem: Nothing in the planned tests runs the app with SPOTIFY_SP_DC set. The code reads `sys.env` directly, the JVM can't set environment variables at runtime, and build.sbt doesn't fork tests or set `Test / envVars`. Slice 1's "same AppConfig with or without SPOTIFY_SP_DC in the source" passes before the change too, because application.conf never mentioned the variable, so it isn't a test that fails without the change. Slice 3's "behave the same whether or not SPOTIFY_SP_DC is in the environment" has no way to put it in the environment. The no-Cookie-header assertion does fail without the change, because the cookie header is always sent today, but it never covers the "even when SPOTIFY_SP_DC is set" part of AC 4, and AC 5 is left to an rg.
findings.suggestion: Either fork the test JVM with `Test / fork := true` and `Test / envVars += "SPOTIFY_SP_DC" -> "<sentinel>"`, then assert that no recorded request has a Cookie header and that the sentinel appears in no request or log line, or say explicitly that AC 5 is shown by the AC 4 test plus the absence of any env read, and get the approver's agreement. Drop the vacuous SP_DC rows from the config table.

findings.problem: The issue's lane says each criterion must be shown by a test that fails without the change. AC 6 (no SPOTIFY_SP_DC in the README, .env.example or how-it-works, and the README calling SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN optional) is left to an `rg` in review. The rg also doesn't check the "optional" wording. The c383e29 commit message gives no reason DocsSpec was removed, so "on purpose" doesn't settle whether this deviation is acceptable.
findings.suggestion: Either add a small test that reads those files (from the project root under sbt) and asserts the absence of `sp_dc` (case-insensitive) and that the README marks SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN as optional, or get the approver to explicitly waive the test requirement for AC 6 and record that in the ADR.

findings.problem: The existing shipped-conf test substitutes values by string-replacing `${KEY}`. Once the key becomes `${?SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN}`, the replace no longer matches, so the "set" row silently loads the default `""`. Optional substitutions are also resolved against the real process environment, so the "unset" row picks up any SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN in the developer's or CI's environment.
findings.suggestion: Replace `${?SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN}` explicitly for the set and empty rows, and assert the resulting `spotify.refreshToken`. For the unset row, resolve with `ConfigResolveOptions.noSystem` or assert only that the config loads.

findings.problem: The plan adds a new `Logs` helper that attaches a logback ListAppender. `testkit.Tls.capturedLogs` and `Tls.logged` already do exactly this, and MainSpec and SpotifyTlsEngineSpec use them.
findings.suggestion: Reuse `Tls.capturedLogs`/`Tls.logged`, filtering on logger name `client.SpotifyClient` and the per-test client_id, or move them to a neutral testkit object without duplicating them.

findings.problem: `initialAuth` stores `resp.refresh_token.getOrElse(creds.refreshToken)`. With the token now optional, that fallback can be `""` (or a token Spotify just rejected), and a later `renew` would then send an empty or rejected refresh token. Spotify normally returns a refresh_token on the authorization-code grant, so this is unlikely, but the design doesn't mention it.
findings.suggestion: After a browser sign-in, use `resp.refresh_token` directly, or fall back to `configuredRefreshToken`, and say which in the ADR.

draft.title: ADR: Start Spotify from SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN, fall back to a retryable browser sign-in, drop the sp_dc cookie
draft.context: `SpotifyClient.initialAuth` requests the authorize URL with `Cookie: sp_dc=$SPOTIFY_SP_DC` (`src/main/scala/client/SpotifyClient.scala:73`). That cookie is a full web session, and it's the only reason a start finishes without a browser. `getOrRefresh` always goes to `initialAuth` when there is no session, so the configured refresh token is never used at startup. `application.conf:4` makes `SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN` required. The code reaches the client through a single `Deferred` (`:176`). After the first callback it stays completed, so a failed code exchange repeats on every poll until the app is restarted. With the cookie gone, the browser is the only fallback, so that has to be fixed too.
draft.decision:
Sign-in stays lazy, at the first Spotify call, so the poll loop and its retry don't change. The `None` branch of `getOrRefresh` calls a new `signIn`:
- **Startup swap**: if `creds.configuredRefreshToken` (trimmed, `None` when blank) is set, `refreshWith("Refresh Token Exchange", token)` posts `grant_type=refresh_token`. Only Spotify's answer about the token itself, **400 with `error: invalid_grant`**, becomes `SpotifyTokenError.Rejected`. That logs a token-free WARN, then runs `initialAuth`. Anything else (429, `invalid_client`, other 4xx, 5xx, transport errors, TLS) is `Failed` or propagates. That poll fails, and the next tick tries the swap again. These failures say nothing about the token, so the user isn't sent to a browser for them.
- **Browser sign-in**: `initialAuth` no longer requests `/authorize` and no longer reads `SPOTIFY_SP_DC`. It calls `codes.attempt`, which opens a fresh wait unless one is still pending, then logs the URL and waits for the code. A failed exchange spends that attempt, so the next tick logs a new URL that can actually be approved. `callbackRoutes` hands the code to `SignInCodes.hand`. The route, port and response stay the same.
- **Session after a browser sign-in**: it stores `resp.refresh_token` directly, never the configured token, which may be blank or just rejected. Spotify always sends a refresh token on the authorization-code grant. If one were missing, the session would hold `""`, and the next renew would fail that poll, the same as a revoked token does today.
- `renew` keeps its current behaviour and goes through `refreshWith("Renew", …)`.
- `SpotifyClient` and `callbackRoutes` keep an overload that takes a `Deferred`, wrapped by `SignInCodes.once`, as a single attempt. Existing callers and tests compile unchanged.
- Order: contracts first, then the retry fix and the startup swap, and only then is the cookie removed. No release makes every start wait on a browser.
draft.components:
- `Main` → `SpotifyClient.resource` (now builds `SignInCodes.make`) → `serverResource(codes)` → `callbackRoutes(codes)` → `codes.hand`.
- `SyncEngine` poller → `getPlaybackState` → `authorised` → `getOrRefresh` → **`signIn`** → `refreshWith("Refresh Token Exchange")` | **`initialAuth`** → `codes.attempt` → `POST accounts.spotify.com/api/token`.
- `renew` → `refreshWith("Renew")`.
- New: `client.SignInCodes` (one code per attempt), and `client.SpotifyTokenError` (sealed) with the pure classifier `of`.
- `domain.spotify.SpotifyCredentials` gains the pure `configuredRefreshToken`.
- Docs: README, `.env.example` and `docs/how-it-works.md` §1. Build: `Test / fork` and `Test / envVars`.
draft.contracts:
- Env `SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN`: required → optional; unset or blank means no token. Additive, because it only loosens.
- Env `SPOTIFY_SP_DC`: no longer read. Removed from `.env.example` and the docs, and any value left in `.env` is ignored. Removal of an optional input.
- Config `spotify.refresh-token`: `refresh-token = ""` followed by `refresh-token = ${?SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN}`. Additive.
- `SpotifyCredentials`: `refreshToken` defaults to `""`, and adds `configuredRefreshToken: Option[String]`. The circe shape is unchanged. Additive.
- New `SpotifyTokenError` (a `RuntimeException`) and new `SignInCodes`. Additive.
- `SpotifyClient`: adds `signIn`. The primary constructor and `callbackRoutes`/`serverResource` now take `SignInCodes[F]`. The `Deferred` overloads remain, so the change is source-compatible. The `"Authorize"` call name goes away and `"Refresh Token Exchange"` is new.
- Outbound HTTP: no `GET /authorize` and no `Cookie` header. Adds one `POST /api/token grant_type=refresh_token` when a token is configured.
- Unchanged: settings JSON, the UI endpoints, the callback route and its port, the scopes.
draft.failureModes:
Carried by `SpotifyTokenError`: `Rejected(call, status, body)` only for 400 with `error=invalid_grant`, and `Failed(call, status, body)` for every other unsuccessful answer.
- **Startup swap**: `Rejected` is recoverable. It logs a WARN, then the browser sign-in runs. `Failed` (429, `invalid_client`, 5xx), transport errors and `SpotifyTlsFailure("Refresh Token Exchange")` fail that poll. The session stays `None`, so the next tick tries the swap again. A wrong client id or secret therefore shows up as a repeated ERROR that names `invalid_client`, and never as a browser loop.
- **Browser sign-in**: a failed code exchange (an expired code, a double click, a 5xx) fails that poll and spends the attempt. The next tick opens a new attempt and logs a new URL, and approving that URL completes sign-in. A callback that arrives with no attempt waiting returns the same page, and the code is dropped. Waiting for approval never times out, which is intended.
- **Renew during a run**: either error fails that poll, as it does today.
- Nothing here is fatal at startup. A missing or blank token can no longer cause a config error.
- Secrets: no token value appears in any message or log line. `body` is Spotify's error JSON, which doesn't echo the token. Never log `SpotifyCredentials` or `AppConfig`.
draft.config: No new settings. `spotify.refresh-token` becomes optional (`""` unless `SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN` is set). pureconfig still requires `client-id` and `client-secret`. A blank or whitespace-only token counts as absent rather than invalid, so `SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN=` copied from `.env.example` works. `LightShowConfig.problems` is untouched.
draft.observability:
All from the `client.SpotifyClient` logger:
- INFO `Signed in to Spotify with the configured refresh token`. No fields.
- WARN `Spotify rejected the configured refresh token (status: <status>); signing in through the browser instead`. Fields: the status only, never the token or the body.
- INFO `Please visit: <authorize URL>` (text unchanged). Fields: `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `scope`, `state`. Logged once per attempt.
- INFO `Signed in to Spotify through the browser`, after a successful code exchange.
- Unchanged: ERROR `Spotify Exchange Failed. Body: <body>`, INFO `Renewed the Spotify access token`, and ERROR `Spotify Poll Failed: <error>` from `SyncEngine`, which carries the call, the status and Spotify's body.
alternatives: Sign in eagerly in `SpotifyClient.resource`: Hue setup would wait on browser approval, and a 5xx at startup would stop the app instead of being retried on the next poll.

`refreshToken: Option[String]`: a more precise type, but every `SpotifyCredentials(...)` call site in four suites would change, and an empty value from `.env` still needs normalising. The default `""` plus `configuredRefreshToken` gives the same behaviour with less change.
Replace the `Deferred` parameter outright instead of keeping overloads: that means rewriting the constructor call in ten places across four suites, purely to change types, inside the same PR.

slices.title: 1. Contracts: optional SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN, SpotifyTokenError, SignInCodes
slices.delivers: `application.conf` gives `refresh-token` a default of `""`, overridden by `${?SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN}`. Adds the `SpotifyCredentials` default and `configuredRefreshToken`, `SpotifyTokenError` with `of`, and the `SignInCodes` type, with `SpotifyClient` keeping its `Deferred` overloads. `renew` raises `SpotifyTokenError` through `refreshWith`. With no token set, the app starts without a config error and signs in through the existing flow.
acceptanceCriteria: The shipped application.conf loads with SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN set (refreshToken = "r"), empty ("") and unset (""), without reading the process environment
`configuredRefreshToken` is None for an empty or whitespace-only token, and otherwise is the trimmed token

`of` gives Rejected only for 400 with error=invalid_grant. It gives Failed for 429, for 400 and 401 with invalid_client, and for every other unsuccessful status. No message contains the refresh token sent
The existing renewal tests pass unchanged: polls keep succeeding after an expired access token is rejected (AC 7)
slices.testStrategy: In LightShowConfigSpec, the shipped-conf test becomes a table. The set and empty rows replace `${?SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN}` explicitly and assert `spotify.refreshToken`. The unset row resolves with `ConfigResolveOptions.noSystem`. ScalaCheck properties cover `configuredRefreshToken` (blank vs non-blank) and `of` (generated statuses × error codes), plus a table with rows for 429, 400 invalid_client, 401 invalid_client, 400 invalid_grant and 503. A further property checks that the message of a renew failure never contains the generated refresh token. SpotifyClientSpec's renewal tests stay as they are.

slices.title: 2. A failed browser sign-in can be retried
slices.delivers: `SignInCodes.make` holds one pending attempt, and a spent one is replaced. `initialAuth` opens an attempt before it logs the URL, and `callbackRoutes` hands the code to the attempt that's waiting. After a failed code exchange, the next poll logs a new URL whose approval completes sign-in, without a restart.
acceptanceCriteria: After a failed code exchange, a second 'Please visit' is logged on the next poll, and handing a second code via /callback leads to a successful poll
The second poll is still waiting until the second code arrives: it doesn't reuse the first code
/callback with no sign-in waiting still answers the same page, and the code is dropped
Existing callback and sign-in tests pass unchanged through the Deferred overloads
slices.testStrategy: In SpotifyClientSpec, use `SignInCodes.make[IO]` with a fake token endpoint that answers 400 to `bad-code` and 200 to `code-2`. The test runs a poll, hands `bad-code`, and asserts that the poll fails. It then starts a second poll in a fiber, checks that the fiber hasn't finished, hands `code-2`, and asserts that playback comes back. ScalaCheck properties over the order of attempt and hand cover SignInCodes: a hand before any attempt gives false, one code per attempt, and a spent attempt is never reused.

slices.title: 3. Start from the configured refresh token
slices.delivers: Adds `signIn`, and the `None` branch of `getOrRefresh` calls it. A valid token starts the lights without a sign-in URL. invalid_grant logs a token-free WARN and falls back to the browser. 429, invalid_client and 5xx are retried on the next poll. The README marks SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN as optional, and how-it-works §1 describes the swap.
acceptanceCriteria: With a valid token, the first poll sends exactly one refresh_token grant, plays, and logs no 'Please visit' (AC 2)

With a 400 invalid_grant answer, there is one WARN that the configured refresh token was rejected, and no log event contains the token value. Then 'Please visit' is logged, and handing a code via /callback leads to a successful poll (AC 3)
With the token unset or empty, no refresh_token grant is sent and 'Please visit' is logged. Handing a code completes sign-in (AC 1)
For a 429, a 401 invalid_client or a 503 answer, the poll fails without logging a sign-in URL, and the next poll tries the swap again
After a browser sign-in, renew sends the refresh token from the code exchange, not the configured one
DocsSpec: the README's SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN row says it's optional
slices.testStrategy: In SpotifyClientSpec, a table of configured token × token-endpoint answer (200, 400 invalid_grant, 429, 401 invalid_client, 503, none), run against a recording fake built with Client.fromHttpApp. Logs come from `Tls.capturedLogs`/`Tls.logged`, filtered on the logger `client.SpotifyClient` and a client_id unique to each test. SyncEngineRunSpec, under TestControl, shows the lights following playback in the valid, rejected and absent cases. Existing sign-in tests switch to `SpotifyCredentials("id", "secret")`. The TLS tests that start with no session expect 'Refresh Token Exchange'. A new DocsSpec reads README.md from the project root.

slices.title: 4. Drop the sp_dc cookie and its docs
slices.delivers: `initialAuth` no longer requests /authorize, and nothing reads SPOTIFY_SP_DC. README, .env.example and how-it-works no longer mention it. build.sbt forks the test JVM with `Test / fork := true` and `Test / envVars += "SPOTIFY_SP_DC" -> "sp-dc-sentinel"`, so the whole suite runs with the variable set.
acceptanceCriteria: A guard test asserts that SPOTIFY_SP_DC equals the sentinel in the test JVM
On every sign-in path (valid, rejected, absent token), no recorded request has a Cookie header or goes to /authorize, and the sentinel appears in no request and no log line (AC 4)
The full suite, sign-in and playback included, passes with SPOTIFY_SP_DC set (AC 5)
DocsSpec: README.md, .env.example and docs/how-it-works.md contain no 'sp_dc' (case-insensitive) (AC 6)
slices.testStrategy: SpotifyClientSpec and SpotifyTlsSpec complete sign-in through `callbackRoutes` instead of a fake /authorize. A table over the three paths checks every recorded request's headers, URI and body, and every captured log message, for the sentinel. The guard test fails if the fork or envVars setting is removed. DocsSpec is extended to cover sp_dc. Every new assertion fails on master, where the cookie is sent and the docs mention it.

```scala
package client

import org.http4s.Status

/** Spotify's token endpoint refused a request. Messages carry Spotify's answer, never the token sent. */
sealed abstract class SpotifyTokenError(message: String) extends RuntimeException(message)

  final case class Rejected(call: String, status: Status, body: String) extends SpotifyTokenError(s"Spotify rejected the $call, $status: $body")

  /** Any other unsuccessful answer, such as 429, `invalid_client` or Spotify being down: says nothing about the token. */
  final case class Failed(call: String, status: Status, body: String) extends SpotifyTokenError(s"Spotify $call failed, $status: $body")

  def of(call: String, status: Status, body: String): SpotifyTokenError = ???
}
```

```scala
package client

import cats.Applicative
import cats.effect.{Concurrent, Deferred}

/** Carries the code from the callback server to the browser sign-in waiting for it, one code per attempt. */
trait SignInCodes[F[_]] {

  /** Opens an attempt, or joins the one still waiting, and gives the wait for its code. A spent attempt is never reused. */
  def attempt: F[F[String]]

  /** Hands over a code from the callback: false if no attempt was waiting for one. */
  def hand(code: String): F[Boolean]
}

object SignInCodes {

  def make[F[_]: Concurrent]: F[SignInCodes[F]] = ???

  /** A single attempt that `deferred` completes. */
  def once[F[_]: Applicative](deferred: Deferred[F, String]): SignInCodes[F] = ???
}
```

findings.section: Slices / 3. Start from the configured refresh token (Tests)
findings.problem: Slice 3 says it will filter captured logs on the `client.SpotifyClient` logger and on a client_id unique to each test. `Tls.capturedLogs` attaches one ListAppender to the root logger, so it collects events from every suite running at the same time. Only the 'Please visit' line contains the client_id, and only because it is part of the URL. The new WARN, the INFO 'Signed in…' lines and the SyncEngine 'Spotify Poll Failed' errors carry no client_id. With that filter, AC 3's 'exactly one WARN that the configured refresh token was rejected' cannot be checked. 'No log event contains the token value' would also check only the 'Please visit' line, so it passes no matter what. The Observability section adds to the confusion by listing client_id/redirect_uri/scope/state as 'fields' when they are only parts of the URL text.
findings.suggestion: Make each test's refresh-token value unique (and its client_id too). Assert the secrecy property over every captured event, of any logger and any level, without filtering. Count the WARN by its message on the `client.SpotifyClient` logger. Either run these suites serially or tie events to the test some other way, such as a per-test MDC or a unique status/body in the fake. Fix the Observability wording so it doesn't describe URL parts as structured fields.

findings.problem: Some existing tests will break in ways the slices don't fully list. `SpotifyTlsEngineSpec` 'signing in on an untrusted certificate…' (src/test/scala/SpotifyTlsEngineSpec.scala:88-103) asserts 'Spotify Authorize failed'. In slice 3 its configured token "refresh" makes the first call 'Refresh Token Exchange'. After slice 4 there is no Authorize call at all, and with a blank token the poll waits for a code instead of failing. In `SpotifyTlsSpec`, the shared `spotify` helper hard-codes `SpotifyCredentials("id","secret","refresh")`. The 'code exchange fails…' test (:95) and the 'trusted sign-in' test (:113) would therefore fail on the refresh swap, or hit the endpoint with `grant_type=refresh_token`, before the code exchange they are meant to test. Saying both 'switch sign-in tests to two-arg creds' and 'TLS tests with no session expect Refresh Token Exchange' doesn't make clear which test gets which.
findings.suggestion: Map each existing no-session test to the path it will exercise: swap (token set) or browser (blank token, code handed through `callbackRoutes`). Name SpotifyTlsEngineSpec:88 explicitly, rename it, and keep TLS coverage for both 'Refresh Token Exchange' and 'Code Exchange'.

findings.problem: After a `Rejected` swap, every later sign-in attempt sends the token Spotify has already rejected again, for example on the next tick after a failed code exchange. Each retry logs the WARN again before a new URL. And with a wrong client secret, or while Spotify is down, the swap is retried on every poll (default 1 s), which logs an ERROR every second with no backoff.
findings.suggestion: Remember for the rest of the run that the configured token was rejected, for example with a `Ref[F, Boolean]` or by clearing it, so later attempts go straight to the browser. Accept the per-poll ERROR for `Failed` in writing as matching how renew behaves today, or note it as a follow-up.

findings.problem: Routing `renew` through `refreshWith` changes its error from `Couldn't renew the Spotify access token, <status>: <body>` to `Spotify Renew failed, …` / `Spotify rejected the Renew…`. So the 'Spotify Poll Failed' ERROR text for in-run renewal failures changes. Observability lists that ERROR as unchanged, and the issue puts renewal changes beyond what the startup exchange needs out of scope.
findings.suggestion: Either keep renew's current message, for example by giving `refreshWith` a message parameter, or list the changed log text under Contracts/Observability.

findings.problem: The scope of `Test / fork := true` and `Test / envVars` isn't stated. They should go on `root` only, not ThisBuild, because `ui` and `model.js` run tests in Node. The guard test that asserts SPOTIFY_SP_DC equals the sentinel also fails whenever the suite runs outside sbt, for example from an IDE runner. Forking also changes how suites run, sequentially by default in one forked JVM, which affects the shared root appender assumptions above.
findings.suggestion: Put both settings in `root`'s `.settings(...)` with a short comment saying why. Accept or document the guard's dependence on sbt, or have it build its own environment.

findings.problem: The `Deferred` overloads on the constructor and on `callbackRoutes` stay in production code only so that tests compile. Through `SignInCodes.once`, their behaviour differs from the real path: no retry, and a spent code is reused. Tests that go through them never exercise `SignInCodes.make`, and the app keeps a second sign-in path that it doesn't use.
findings.suggestion: Either move the existing sign-in tests onto `SignInCodes.make`/`once` while slices 2 and 4 rewrite them anyway, and drop the overloads, or state that the overloads exist only for tests and are not covered by the retry guarantees.

findings.problem: The lane requires each criterion to be shown by a test that fails without the change. AC 7 (renewal still works) is a non-regression covered by existing renewal tests that pass on master too, so it can't satisfy that wording as stated.
findings.suggestion: Say outright that AC 7 is covered by the existing renewal tests as a regression guard. Or add a renewal test after each new sign-in path, for example a renew after a startup swap that returned no new refresh_token, which uses code that is new in this change.
